So that servant came and showed his lord these things. Then the master of the house, being angry, said to his servant, ‘Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in hither the poor, and the maimed, and the halt, and the blind.’
And the servant said, ‘Lord, it is done as thou hast commanded, and yet there is room.’
And the lord said unto the servant, ‘Go out into the highways and hedges, and compel them to come in, that my house may be filled.’
For I say unto you, that none of those men which were bidden shall taste of my supper.”

sections.title: Concerning the following of the Lord.

verses.text: And after this, many people went together, and He said to them, "If anyone comes to Me, and does not hate his father and mother, his wife and children, his brothers and sisters, yes, and his own life also, he cannot be My disciple."
"And whoever does not bear his cross and come after Me cannot be My disciple."
"For which of you, intending to build a tower, does not sit down first and count the cost, whether he has enough to finish it?"

sections.title: A parable concerning the man who builds a house.

verses.text: "If among you there be one who desires to build a house, let him consider who is able to accomplish it, for who is he that does not think beforehand of the cost?"
"Let all who see that the foundation is laid and the work is begun, consider it as a matter of great importance."
"This man has begun to work; yet they will say, 'He has begun to lay the foundation, but is unable to finish.'"

"If a king desires to go against another king, let him first sit down and consider whether he is able with ten thousand to meet him that cometh against him with twenty thousand; for it is wise to deliberate before engaging in such matters."
"Yet, even so, while he is still afar off, he sendeth messengers to ask for peace."
"Thus, if among you there be one who is not of the world, even if he possess wealth, he shall not be able to become a servant of the Lord."
"Salt is good; but if the salt have lost its savor, wherewith shall it be seasoned?"
"Whether it be for the earth or for the fowl, it shall not be fit; but behold, they shall be cast out; let him that hath ears to hear, hear."

sections.title: Concerning the parable of the steward.

verses.text: And the publicans and sinners drew near unto Him to hear Him.
And the scribes and Pharisees murmured, saying, “This man receiveth sinners, and eateth with them.”
Thus they spake against Him.
“What man of you, having a hundred sheep, if he lose one of them, doth not leave the ninety and nine in the wilderness, and go after that which is lost until he find it?”
And when he hath found it, he layeth it on his shoulders, rejoicing.
And when he cometh home, he calleth together his friends and neighbors, saying unto them, “Rejoice with me; for I have found my sheep which was lost.”
I say unto you, that likewise joy shall be in heaven over one sinner that repenteth, more than over ninety and nine just persons, which need no repentance.

sections.title: And it came to pass concerning the woman who was lost.

verses.text: "If a woman has ten coins and loses one, will she not light a lamp and sweep the house, seeking diligently until she finds it?"
"And when she has found it, she will call her friends and neighbors together, saying, 'Rejoice with me, for I have found the coin which I had lost.'"
"I say to you, likewise, there will be joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner who repents."

sections.title: And there was a man who had two sons.

verses.text: ዳግመኛም እንዲህ አለ፥ “አንድ ሰው ሁለት ልጆች ነበሩት።
ታናሹ ልጁም አባቱን፦ ‘አባቴ ሆይ፥ ከገንዘብህ የሚደርሰኝን ከፍለህ ስጠኝ’ አለው፤ ገንዘቡንም ከፍሎ ሰጠው።
ከጥቂት ቀን በኋላም ያ ትንሹ ልጁ ገንዘቡን ሁሉ ሰብስቦ ወደ ሩቅ ሀገር ሄደ፤ በዚያም በመዳራት እየኖረ ገንዘቡን ሁሉ በተነ፤ አጠፋም።
ገንዘቡንም ሁሉ በጨረሰ ጊዜ፥ በዚያ ሀገር ጽኑ ራብ መጣ፤ እርሱም ተቸገረ።
ሄዶም ከዚያ ሀገር ሰዎች ለአንዱ ተቀጠረ፤ እሪያዎችንም ይጠብቅ ዘንድ ወደ እርሻው ቦታ ሰደደው።
እሪያዎች ከሚመገቡት ተረንቃሞም ይጠግብ ዘንድ ተመኘ፤ ግን የሚሰጠው አልነበረም።
በልቡም እንዲህ ብሎ ዐሰበ፦ እህል የሚተርፋቸው የአባቴ ሠራተኞች ምን ያህል ናቸው? እኔ ግን በዚህ በረኃብ ልሞት ነው።
ተነሥቼ ወደ አባቴ ልሂድና እንዲህ ልበለው፦ ‘አባቴ ሆይ፥ በሰማይም፥ በፊትህም በደልሁ።
እንግዲህ ወዲህስ ልጅህ ልባል አይገባኝም፤ ከአገልጋዮችህ እንደ አንዱ አድርገኝ።’
ተነሥቶም ወደ አባቱ ሄደ፤ አባቱም ከሩቅ አየውና ራራለት፤ ሮጦም አንገቱን አቅፎ ሳመው።
And he said, "Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you; I am no longer worthy to be called your son; make me as one of your hired servants."
And his father said to the servants, "Bring quickly the best robes and put them on him; and put a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet."
Bring the fatted calf and kill it; and let us eat and be merry.
For this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found." And they began to be merry.
"Now his elder son was in the field; and as he came and drew near to the house, he heard music and dancing."
And he called one of the servants and asked what these things meant.
And he said to him, "Your brother has come, and your father has killed the fatted calf, because he has received him safe and sound."
But he was angry and would not go in. Therefore his father came out and pleaded with him.

So he answered and said to his father, "Lo, these many years I have been serving you; I never transgressed your commandment at any time; and yet you never gave me a young goat, that I might make merry with my friends."
But as soon as this son of yours came, who has devoured your livelihood with harlots, you killed the fatted calf for him."
And the father said, "My son, thou art ever with me; all that I have is thine."
But behold, this thy brother was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found."

sections.title: Concerning the mighty one, the conqueror.

verses.text: ጌታችን ኢየሱስም ለደቀ መዛሙርቱ እንዲህ አላቸው፥ “መጋቢ የነበረው አንድ ባለጸጋ ሰው ነበረ፤ ገንዘቡን ሁሉ እንደሚበትን አድርገው በእርሱ ዘንድ ከሰሱት።
ጌታውም ጠርቶ፦ ‘በአንተ ላይ የምሰማው ይህ ነገር ምንድን ነው? እንግዲህ ወዲህ ለእኔ መጋቢ ልትሆን አትችልምና የመጋቢነትህን ሂሳብ አስረክበኝ’ አለው።
ያም መጋቢ ዐስቦ እንዲህ አለ፦ ‘ምን ላድርግ? አሁን ጌታዬ ከመጋቢነቴ ይሽረኛል፤ ማረስ አልችልም፤ ለመለመንም አፍራለሁ።
እንግዲህ ጌታዬ ከምግብናዬ የሻረኝ እንደ ሆነ በቤታቸው ይቀበሉኝ ዘንድ የማደርገውን እኔ ዐውቃለሁ።’
ለጌታውም ዕዳ የሚከፍሉትን ጠራቸው፤ የመጀመሪያውንም፦ ‘ለጌታዬ የምትከፍለው ዕዳ ምን ያህል ነው?’ አለው፤ እርሱም፦ ‘መቶ ማድጋ ዘይት ነው’ አለው።
‘እነሆ፥ ደብዳቤህ፤ ተቀምጠህ አምሳ ማድጋ አለብኝ ብለህ ፈጥነህ ጻፍ’ አለው።
ሁለተኛውንም፦ ‘አንተሳ ለጌታዬ የምትከፍለው ዕዳ ምን ያህል ነው?’ አለው፤ እርሱም፦ ‘መቶ ማድጋ ስንዴ ነው’ አለው፤ ‘እነሆ፥ ደብዳቤህ፤ ተቀምጠህ ሰማንያ አለብኝ ብለህ ፈጥነህ ጻፍ’ አለው።
ጌታውም ዐመፀኛውን መጋቢ እንደ ብልህ ሰው ስለ ሠራ አመሰገነው፤ ከብርሃን ልጆች ይልቅ የዚህ ዓለም ልጆች በዓለማቸው ይራቀቃሉና።
እኔም እላችኋለሁ፦ ባለቀባችሁ ጊዜ እነርሱ በዘለዓለም ቤታቸው ይቀበሉአችሁ ዘንድ በዐመፃ ገንዘብ ለእናንተ ወዳጆች አድርጉበት።
“በጥቂት የሚታመን በብዙ ይታመናል፤ በጥቂት የሚያምፅም በብዙም ቢሆን ያምፃል።
በዐመፃ ገንዘብ ካልታመናችሁ በእውነተኛው ገንዘብ ማን ያምናችኋል?
በሌላውስ ገንዘብ ካልታመናችሁ የራሱን ማን ይሰጣችኋል?
ለሁለት ጌቶች መገዛት የሚችል አገልጋይ የለም፤ ካልሆነም አንዱን ይወድዳል፤ ሁለተኛውንም ይጠላል፤ ወይም ለአንዱ ይታዘዛል፤ ለሁለተኛውም እንቢ ይላል፤ እንዲሁም እናንተ ገንዘብ እየወደዳችሁ ለእግዚአብሔር መገዛት አትችሉም።”
ገንዘብን የሚወዱ ፈሪሳውያንም ይህን ሁሉ ነገር ሰምተው ተጠቃቀሱበት።
እርሱም፥ “እናንተስ ለሰው ይምሰል ትመጻደቃላችሁ፤ እግዚአብሔርም ልቡናችሁን ያውቃል፤ በሰው ዘንድ የከበረ በእግዚአብሔር ዘንድ የተናቀ ይሆናልና።

sections.title: Concerning the Oracles and Concerning the Prophets

verses.text: "The Law and the Prophets were until John; since that time the kingdom of God is preached, and every man presseth into it."
"But it is easier for heaven and earth to pass, than one tittle of the law to fail."
"Whosoever shall put away his wife, and marry another, committeth adultery; and whosoever marrieth her that is put away from her husband committeth adultery."

sections.title: Concerning one who is rich and concerning Lazarus.

verses.text: "There was a certain rich man; he was clothed in purple and fine linen, and he feasted sumptuously every day."
"And there was a certain beggar named Lazarus, full of sores, who was laid at the rich man's gate."
"Desiring to be fed with the crumbs which fell from the rich man's table; moreover, the dogs came and licked his sores."
"So it was that the beggar died, and was carried by the angels to Abraham's bosom; the rich man also died and was buried."
"And being in torments in Hades, he lifted up his eyes and saw Abraham afar off, and Lazarus in his bosom."
"Then he cried and said, 'Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus that he may dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue; for I am tormented in this flame.'"
"But Abraham said, 'Son, remember that in your lifetime you received your good things, and likewise Lazarus evil things; but now he is comforted and you are tormented.'"
"And besides all this, between us and you there is a great gulf fixed, so that those who want to pass from here to you cannot, nor can those from there pass to us.'"
"Then he said, 'I beg you therefore, father, that you would send him to my father's house.'"
"For I have five brothers, that he may testify to them, lest they also come to this place of torment.'"
And Abraham said, "Moses and the prophets are with them; let them hear them."
And he said, "Nay; father Abraham, if one go unto them from the dead, they will not be persuaded, though one rose from the dead."
And Abraham said, "If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead."

sections.title: Concerning the coming of destruction.

verses.text: Our Lord Jesus said to His disciples, "Woe unto the man through whom temptation cometh; it were better for him that a millstone were hanged about his neck, and he were cast into the sea."
It is better for a man to be cast into the depths of the sea with a millstone about his neck than to cause one of these little ones to stumble.
Take heed to yourselves; if your brother trespass against you, rebuke him; and if he repent, forgive him.
And if he trespass against you seven times in a day, and seven times in a day turn again to you, saying, 'I repent,' thou shalt forgive him."

sections.title: Concerning the strength of faith.

verses.text: And the apostles said unto the Lord, "Increase our faith."

Our Lord Jesus said unto them, "If ye have faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye might say unto this sycamine tree, Be thou plucked up by the root, and be thou planted in the sea; and it should obey you."

sections.title: Concerning the commandment.

verses.text: "Who among you is a servant that tends to the vine or the cattle? Is it not the master who returns from the field? Hurry, come here, and sit at the table with me."
"Prepare my meal, that I may eat and drink; and when I have eaten and drunk, you shall be satisfied. After this, will you say to me, 'Eat and drink,' or will you not?"
"Thus, if the master commands and the servant performs his duty, is there not gratitude owed to that servant?"
"Likewise, you also should say, 'We are unworthy servants; we have only done what was our duty to do.'"

sections.title: The ten shall be as a refuge for the oppressed.

verses.text: And after this, as He journeyed toward Jerusalem, He passed through the midst of Samaria and Galilee.
And as He entered into a certain village, there met Him ten men that were lepers, who stood afar off.
And they lifted up their voices and said, “Jesus, Master, have mercy on us.”
And when He saw them, He said unto them, “Go show yourselves unto the priests.” And it came to pass, that, as they went, they were cleansed.
And one of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back, and with a loud voice glorified God.
And fell down on his face at His feet, giving Him thanks: and he was a Samaritan.
And Jesus answering said, “Were there not ten cleansed? But where are the nine?
There are not found that returned to give glory to God, save this stranger.”
And He said unto him, “Arise, go thy way: thy faith hath made thee whole.”

sections.title: Concerning the coming of the kingdom of God.

verses.text: And the Pharisees asked Him, saying, "When will the kingdom of God come?" He answered them, "The kingdom of God does not come with observation.
Nor will they say, 'See here!' or 'See there!' For indeed, the kingdom of God is within you."
And He said to His disciples, "The days will come when you will desire to see one of the days of the Son of Man, and you will not see it."
And they will say to you, 'Look here!' or 'Look there!' Do not go after them or follow them.
For as the lightning that flashes out of one part under heaven shines to the other part under heaven, so also the Son of Man will be in His day.
But first He must suffer many things and be rejected by this generation.
And as it was in the days of Noah, so it will be also in the days of the Son of Man.
They ate, they drank, they married wives, they were given in marriage, until the day that Noah entered the ark, and the flood came and destroyed them all.
Likewise as it was also in the days of Lot: They ate, they drank, they bought, they sold, they planted, they built;
But on the day that Lot went out of Sodom, it rained fire and brimstone from heaven and destroyed them all.
The son of man shall be as it is in the day of his coming; he shall not be known.
At that time, he who is in heaven shall not descend to take his wealth from the house on earth; he who is in the field shall not turn back.
Remember Lot's wife.
He who loves his life shall lose it; but he who loses his life for my sake shall keep it.
I tell you: Two shall be in one bed; one shall be taken, and the other shall be left.
Two women shall be grinding together; one shall be taken, and the other shall be left.
Two men shall be in one field; one shall be taken, and the other shall be left.”
And they answered, saying, “Lord, where?” And he said to them, “Wherever the body is, there the eagles will be gathered together.”

sections.title: A parable concerning prayer without ceasing.

verses.text: ዘወትር እንዲጸልዩ፥ እንዳይሰለቹም በምሳሌ ነገራቸው።
እንዲህም አላቸው፥ “በአንዲት ከተማ እግዚአብሔርን የማይፈራ፥ ሰውንም የማያፍር አንድ ዳኛ ነበር።
በዚያችም ከተማ አንዲት መበለት ነበረች፤ ዕለት ዕለትም ወደ እርሱ እየመጣች ከባለጋራዬ ፍረድልኝ ትለው ነበር።
እንቢ ብሎም አዘገያት። ከዚህም በኋላ በልቡ ዐስቦ እንዲህ አለ፦ ‘ምንም እግዚአብሔርን ባልፈራ፥ ሰውንም ባላፍር
ይህቺ ሴት እንዳትዘበዝበኝ፥ ዘወትርም እየመጣች እንዳታታክተኝ እፈርድላታለሁ’።”
ጌታችንም እንዲህ አላቸው፥ “ዐመፀኛው ዳኛ ያለውን ስሙ።
እንግዲህ እግዚአብሔር በመዓልትና በሌሊት ወደ እርሱ ለሚጮኹ ለወዳጆቹ አይፈርድምን? ወይስ ቸል ይላቸዋልን?
እላችኋለሁ ፈጥኖ ይፈርድላቸዋል፤ ነገር ግን የሰው ልጅ በመጣ ጊዜ በምድር ላይ እምነትን ያገኝ ይሆን?”

sections.title: Concerning the Pharisee and the Publican.

verses.text: They are like those who would justify themselves and condemn their neighbors.
"Two men went up to the temple to pray; one was a Pharisee, and the other a tax collector.
The Pharisee stood and prayed thus with himself: 'God, I thank You that I am not like other men, extortioners, unjust, adulterers, or even as this tax collector.
I fast twice a week; I give tithes of all that I possess.'
And the tax collector, standing afar off, would not so much as raise his eyes to heaven, but beat his breast, saying, 'God, be merciful to me a sinner!'
I tell you, this man went down to his house justified rather than the other; for everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and he who humbles himself will be exalted."

sections.title: Our Lord, concerning the children, for I have taken them away.

verses.text: And they brought unto Him children, that He might touch them; but the disciples rebuked them.
But Jesus called them unto Him, and said, “Suffer little children to come unto Me, and forbid them not; for of such is the kingdom of God.”
Verily I say unto you, Whosoever shall not receive the kingdom of God as a little child shall in no wise enter therein.”

sections.title: Concerning the matter of life.

verses.text: And one ruler asked Him, "Good Teacher, what good deed must I do to inherit eternal life?"
Our Lord Jesus answered him, saying, "Why do you call me good? No one is good except One, that is, God."
"You know the commandments: 'Do not murder; do not commit adultery; do not steal; do not bear false witness; honor your father and your mother.'"
He said to Him, "All these things I have kept from my youth up."
Our Lord Jesus, hearing this, said to him, "You lack one thing: go, sell all that you have and distribute to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me."
But he heard this and became very sorrowful, for he was very rich.
Our Lord Jesus, seeing that he became very sorrowful, said, "How hard it is for those who have riches to enter the kingdom of God!
For it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God."
And those who heard it said, "Who then can be saved?"
He replied, "The things which are impossible with men are possible with God."

sections.title: The Inquiry of Peter

verses.text: And Peter said, "Behold, we have left all things and followed Thee; what then shall we have?"
And He answered them, "Verily I say unto you, there is no man that hath left house, or brethren, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, for the sake of the kingdom of God,
who shall not receive manifold more in this present time, and in the world to come life everlasting."

sections.title: Concerning sickness and concerning death.

verses.text: And He sent forth the twelve, saying unto them, “Behold, we go up to Jerusalem; and all things that are written by the prophets shall be accomplished concerning the Son of man.
They shall deliver Him unto the Gentiles; and they shall mock Him, and shall scourge Him, and shall spit upon Him.
And they shall kill Him; and the third day He shall rise again.”
But they understood not this saying, and it was hid from them, that they perceived it not; and they feared to ask Him concerning that saying.

sections.title: Concerning the blind man who was in Jericho.

verses.text: And as they approached Jericho, a certain blind man sat by the wayside begging.
And hearing the multitude pass by, he asked, “What is this that I hear?”
They said unto him, “Jesus of Nazareth passeth by.”
And he cried out, saying, “Jesus, thou son of David, have mercy on me.”
And they which went before rebuked him, that he should hold his peace; but he cried so much the more, “Thou son of David, have mercy on me.”
And our Lord Jesus stood still and commanded him to be brought unto him.
And when he was come near, he asked him, saying, “What wilt thou that I shall do unto thee?” And he said, “Lord, that I may receive my sight.”
And Jesus said unto him, “Receive thy sight; thy faith hath saved thee.”
And immediately he received his sight, and glorified God; and all the people, when they saw it, gave praise unto God.

sections.title: Concerning Zacchaeus the Tax Collector

verses.text: Our Lord Jesus was passing through Jericho.
Behold, there was a man named Zacchaeus, who was a chief among the publicans; and he was rich.
And he sought to see Jesus, who he was; and could not for the press, because he was of little stature.
And he ran before, and climbed up into a sycamore tree to see him: for he was to pass that way.
And when Jesus came to the place, he looked up and saw him, and said unto him, “Zacchaeus, make haste, and come down; for today I must abide at thy house.”
And he made haste, and came down, and received him joyfully.
And when they saw it, they all murmured, saying, “He is gone to be guest with a man that is a sinner.”
And Zacchaeus stood and said unto the Lord, “Behold, Lord, the half of my goods I give to the poor; and if I have taken anything from any man by false accusation, I restore him fourfold.”
And Jesus said unto him, “This day is salvation come to this house, forsomuch as he also is a son of Abraham.”
For the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost.”

sections.title: A parable concerning those who received ten.

verses.text: And when they heard this, they spoke to one another in parables, for they were drawing near to Jerusalem; and they said, "This is the kingdom of God that is about to be revealed to us."
Thus He said, "A certain nobleman went into a far country to receive for himself a kingdom and to return."
He called ten of his servants and delivered to them ten minas, and said to them, 'Do business till I come back.'
But the citizens of his country hated him and sent a delegation after him, saying, 'We will not have this man to reign over us.'

And so it was that when he returned, having received the kingdom, he ordered those servants to whom he had given the money to be called to him, that he might know how much every man had gained by trading.
Then came the first, saying, 'Master, your mina has earned ten minas more.'
And the master said to him, 'Well done, good servant; because you were faithful in a very little, have authority over ten cities.'
Then the second came, saying, 'Master, your mina has earned five minas.'
Likewise he said to him, 'You also be over five cities.'

Then another came, saying, 'Master, here is your mina, which I have kept put away in a handkerchief; for I feared you because you are an austere man. You collect what you did not deposit and reap what you did not sow.'
I am troubled because I know that you are a man who takes what is not yours, who seizes what is not sown, and who gathers what is not gathered.

And the Lord said, "Do you not know that you are a wicked servant, who takes what I have not deposited, who seizes what I have not sown, and who gathers what I have not scattered? According to your word, I will judge you."
Why did you not bring my money to the exchangers? I also came and was with the profit that I had made.
Then they stood and said, "Who among you has received from him ten? To whom shall we give?"
And they said, "Lord, is there not one who has ten?"
He answered them, saying, "To everyone who has, more will be given; and from him who does not have, even what he has will be taken away."
But bring those enemies of mine who did not want me to reign over them here, and slay them before me."

sections.title: And concerning His entrance into Jerusalem.

verses.text: ይህንም ተናግሮ ወደ ፊት ሄደ፤ ወደ ኢየሩሳሌምም ወጣ።
ደብረ ዘይት ወደሚባል ተራራ አጠገብ ወዳሉት ወደ ቤተ ፋጌና ወደ ቢታንያ በቀረበ ጊዜ፥ ከደቀ መዛሙርቱ ሁለቱን ላከ።
እንዲህም አላቸው፥ “በፊታችሁ ወደ አለችው መንደር ሂዱ፤ ገብታችሁም ሰው ያልተቀመጠበት የታሰረ ውርንጫ ታገኛላችሁ፤ ፈትታችሁም አምጡልኝ።
ለምን ትፈቱታላችሁ? የሚላችሁ ቢኖር ጌታው ይሻዋል በሉ።”
የተላኩትም ሄደው እንደ አላቸው አገኙ።
ውርንጫውንም ሲፈቱ ባለቤቶቹ “ውርንጫውን ለምን ትፈቱታላችሁ?” አሉአቸው።
እነርሱም “ጌታው ይሻዋል” አሉ።
ይዘውም ወደ ጌታችን ኢየሱስ ወሰዱት፤ በውርንጫው ላይም ልብሳቸውን ጭነው ጌታችን ኢየሱስን በዚያ ላይ አስቀመጡት።
ሲሄዱም በመንገድ ልብሳቸውን አነጠፉ።
ወደ ደብረ ዘይት ዐቀበት መውረጃም በደረሱ ጊዜ፥ ደቀ መዛሙርቱ በሙሉ ስለ አዩት ኀይል ሁሉ ደስ ይላቸውና እግዚአብሔርን በታላቅ ቃል ያመሰግኑት ዘንድ ጀመሩ።
Thus it is said, "Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord; blessed is the King of Israel; peace on earth, and glory in the highest."
And among the people, from the Pharisees, there were those who said, "Teacher, rebuke your disciples."
And He answered them, saying, "I tell you that if these should keep silent, the stones would immediately cry out."

sections.title: Concerning the Destruction of Jerusalem

verses.text: And when the time came, He beheld the city and wept over it.
Thus He said, "If you had known, even you, especially in this your day, the things that make for your peace! But now they are hidden from your eyes.
For the days will come upon you when your enemies will lay siege to you; they will encircle you and press hard against you on every side;
and they will dash you to the ground, and your children within you; and they will not leave in you one stone upon another, because you did not know the time of your visitation."

sections.title: Our Lord, for casting out the merchants from the house of the temple.

verses.text: And He entered the temple, and there He cast out all those who sold and bought therein; and He overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of them that sold doves.
"My house shall be called a house of prayer," thus it is written; "but ye have made it a den of thieves."
And it was customary that the priests, the chief men, the scribes, and the great ones of the people should be taught in the temple; they were to be admonished therein.
Nevertheless, they did what they pleased; for the people were all gathered to hear the teaching and were filled with admiration.

sections.title: A question presented by the priests.

verses.text: And after this, on one day, as the people were being taught in the temple, and as the gospel was being proclaimed to them, the chief priests, the scribes, and the elders rose up against Him.
"By what authority do You do this? Who gave You this authority to do these things? Tell us," they said.
But He answered them, "I also will ask you one question; answer me, and I will tell you by what authority I do these things."
"The baptism of John, was it from heaven or from men?" they discussed among themselves.
And they reasoned among themselves, saying, "If we say, 'From heaven,' He will say, 'Why then did you not believe him?'
But if we say, 'From men,' all the people will stone us, for they are convinced that John was a prophet."
So they answered that they did not know where it was from.
And Jesus said to them, "Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things."

sections.title: Concerning the keepers of the vine.

verses.text: And to the people, He began to speak this parable, saying: “A certain man planted a vineyard, and he set a hedge about it, and dug a winepress, and built a tower, and let it out to husbandmen, and went into a far country, and did not return.

And when the season of the fruits drew near, he sent his servants to the husbandmen, that they might receive the fruits of the vineyard. But the husbandmen took his servants, and beat one, and killed another, and stoned another.
Again he sent other servants more than the first, and they did likewise unto them.
And last of all he sent unto them his son, saying, They will reverence my son.
But when the husbandmen saw the son, they said among themselves, This is the heir; come, let us kill him, and let us seize on his inheritance.
And they caught him, and cast him out of the vineyard, and slew him.
When the lord therefore of the vineyard cometh, what will he do unto those husbandmen?
They say unto him, He will miserably destroy those wicked men, and will let out his vineyard unto other husbandmen, which shall render him the fruits in their seasons.
Jesus said unto them, Did ye never read in the scriptures, The stone which the builders rejected, the same is become the head of the corner? This is the Lord's doing, and it is marvelous in our eyes?
Therefore say I unto you, The kingdom of God shall be taken from you, and given to a nation bringing forth the fruits thereof.”
At that time, the leaders of the priests and the scribes sought to lay hands on Him; for they knew that He was speaking of them. However, they feared the people.

sections.title: Concerning the giving of tribute to Caesar.

verses.text: And after they had departed from among them, they prepared that which they would keep; and they sent forth those who would bring forth their own offerings unto the priests and unto the Levites, that they might give unto him.
And they asked him, saying, “Teacher, thou speakest the truth, and teachest the way of God in truth; neither carest thou for any man: for thou regardest not the person of men.”
“Is it lawful to give tribute unto Caesar, or not?”
But he perceived their wickedness, and said, “Why tempt ye me? Show me the tribute money.”
And they brought unto him a penny. And he saith unto them, “Whose is this image and superscription?” They said unto him, “Caesar's.”
Then saith he unto them, “Render therefore unto Caesar the things which are Caesar's; and unto God the things that are God's.”
And they could not take hold of his words before the people: and they marvelled at his answer, and held their peace.

sections.title: Concerning the resurrection of the dead.

verses.text: "The dead do not rise," some of the Sadducees said to Him.
And they asked Him, saying, "Teacher, Moses wrote to us, 'If a man dies having no children, his brother should take his wife and raise up offspring for his brother.'"
Now there were seven brothers; and the first took a wife, and he died without children.
Likewise, the second also, and he died childless;
and the third took her, and in like manner the seven also; they left no children and died.
Last of all, the woman died also.
Therefore, in the resurrection, whose wife does she become? For all seven had her as wife."
Jesus answered and said to them, "The sons of this age marry and are given in marriage;
but those who are counted worthy to attain that age and the resurrection from the dead neither marry nor are given in marriage,
nor can they die anymore, for they are equal to the angels and are sons of God, being sons of the resurrection."
The Lord said, "I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob," thus speaking to Moses as it is written in the Scriptures.
For He is the God of the living, not the God of the dead; for all are alive unto Him.
And those who were of the scribes answered, saying, "Teacher, you have spoken well."
From that time forth, no one dared to ask Him any more questions.

sections.title: Concerning the inquiry presented regarding the Messiah.

verses.text: And thus they said, “How can Christ be called the son of David?
He Himself declared in the Book of Psalms, ‘The Lord said unto my Lord, Sit thou on my right hand,
Until I make thine enemies thy footstool.’
Therefore, how can He be the son of David, when David himself calleth Him ‘my Lord’?”

sections.title: Concerning the admonition of the holy psalmist.

verses.text: And the people, when they heard, said unto their priests, thus:

"Let us not be found in our garments, nor in this manner, for those who seek to ascend in the marketplace and stand face to face in the assembly, and in the time of gathering, to take their place in the seat of honor, let them beware of the writings of those who desire such."
"Those who consume the wealth of the needy, and for the sake of gain neglect prayer, they shall receive this great judgment."

sections.title: Two men contended concerning a poor woman.

verses.text: በሙዳየ ምጽዋቱ መባቸውን የሚያገቡ ባለጠጎችን አየ።
አንዲት ድሃ መበለትም ሁለት መሐለቅ ስታስገባ አየ።
እንዲህም አላቸው፥ “እውነት እላችኋለሁ፥ ይህቺ ድሃ መበለት ከሁሉ ይልቅ አብዝታ ለእግዚአብሔር መባ አገባች።
እነዚህ ሁሉ ከተረፋቸው ለእግዚአብሔር መባ አግብተዋልና፤ ይህቺ ግን ከድህነቷ ያላትን ጥሪቷን ሁሉ አገባች።”

sections.title: Concerning Jerusalem and the House of the Sanctuary.

verses.text: ስለ ቤተ መቅደስም ድንጋዩ ያማረ ነው፥ አሠራሩም ያጌጠ ነው የሚሉት ነበሩ።
እንዲህም አላቸው፥ “ይህን ታያላችሁን? በእዚህ ቦታ ድንጋይ በድንጋይ ላይ የማይተውበትና ሳይፈርስ የማይቀርበት ዘመን ይመጣል።”
እነርሱም፥ “መምህር ሆይ፥ ይህ መቼ ይደረጋል? ይህስ የሚሆንበት ጊዜው፥ ምልክቱስ ምንድን ነው?” ብለው ጠየቁት።
እርሱም እንዲህ አላቸው፥ “ብዙዎች እኔ ክርስቶስ ነኝ፤ ጊዜውም ደርሶአል እያሉ በስሜ ይመጣሉና እንዳያስቱአችሁ ተጠንቀቁ፤ እነርሱንም ተከትላችሁ አትሂዱ።
ጦርነትንና ጠብን፥ ክርክርንም በሰማችሁ ጊዜ አትደንግጡ፤ አስቀድሞ ይህ ይሆን ዘንድ ግድ ነውና፤ ነገር ግን ወዲያው የሚፈጸም አይደለም።”
እንዲህም አላቸው፥ “ሕዝብ በሕዝብ ላይ፥ ነገሥታትም በነገሥታት ላይ ይነሣሉ።
በየሀገሩ ታላቅ የምድር መነዋወጥና ራብ፥ በሰውም ላይ በሽታና ፍርሀት ይመጣል፤ በሰማይም ታላቅ ምልክት ይሆናል።
ከዚህም ሁሉ አስቀድሞ ይይዙአችኋል፤ ወደ አደባባዮችም ይወስዱአችኋል፤ ያሳድዱአችኋል፤ ያስሩአችኋል፤ ስለ ስሜም ወደ ነገሥታትና ወደ መሳፍንት ይወስዱአችኋል።
ይህም በእነርሱ ላይ ምስክር ይሆንባቸዋል።
ዕወቁ፤ የምትናገሩትንም በልባችሁ አታስቡ።
And I shall give you wisdom and understanding, that they may not rise against you nor be able to harm you.
Your fathers and your brethren, and your friends and your companions shall surely give unto you.
All shall call upon you for my name; they shall also seek to harm you.
Yet, from among yourselves, let not even one be lost.
In your patience, your souls shall be preserved.

sections.title: Concerning the Destruction of Jerusalem

verses.text: "When the time comes that you are not able to escape from Jerusalem, know that its destruction has come upon it."
"At that time, let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains; and let those who are in the midst of it depart out; and let not those who are in the country enter therein."
"For all that is written concerning it shall be fulfilled, for it is the time of its visitation."
"But woe unto them that are with child, and to them that give suck in those days! For there shall be great distress in the land, and wrath upon this people."
"And they shall fall by the edge of the sword; and shall be led away captive into all nations; and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled."

sections.title: Concerning the coming of Christ and the signs thereof.

verses.text: "And there shall be signs in the sun and in the moon, and in the stars; and upon the earth distress of nations, with perplexity; the sea and the waves roaring."
"Men's hearts failing them for fear, and for looking after those things which are coming on the earth: for the powers of heaven shall be shaken."
"And then shall they see the Son of man coming in a cloud with power and great glory."
"And when these things begin to come to pass, then look up, and lift up your heads; for your redemption draweth nigh."
"But take heed to yourselves, lest at any time your hearts be overcharged with surfeiting and drunkenness, and cares of this life, and so that day come upon you unawares."
"For as a snare shall it come on all them that dwell on the face of the whole earth."
"Watch ye therefore, and pray always, that ye may be accounted worthy to escape all these things that shall come to pass, and to stand before the Son of man."
"And he spake to them a parable; Behold the fig tree, and all the trees;"
"When they now shoot forth, ye see and know of your own selves that summer is now nigh at hand."

sections.title: Teaching and counsel

verses.text: "Take heed to yourselves; do not let your hearts be weighed down with dissipation and drunkenness, and the cares of this life, for that day will come upon you suddenly like a snare."
"For it will come upon all those who dwell on the face of the whole earth."
"Therefore, be watchful in prayer, that you may be able to stand before the Son of Man at all times."

sections.title: Concerning the dwelling of the olive.

verses.text: Day by day he was taught in the temple; but by night he would go out and abide in the mount called the Mount of Olives.
And all the people came early in the morning to him in the temple, to hear him.

sections.title: The chief priests sought to put the Lord to death as they desired.

verses.text: And the feast which is called Passover drew near.
And the chief priests and the scribes sought how they might kill Him; but they feared the people.

sections.title: Judah, having conspired against the Lord, sought to betray Him as it was agreed.

verses.text: The number was two and twenty, and in their assembly, the heart of Judah was stirred up by Satan.
And he went and spoke to the chief priests and the rulers, that they might deliver him up.
And they rejoiced and agreed to give him thirty pieces of silver.
And he said, "I will do it"; for it was a fitting time for him to be delivered up, even when there was no man present.

sections.title: Concerning the preparation of the Passover.

verses.text: The time of the Passover lamb has come, which is the feast of unleavened bread.
Our Lord Jesus said to Peter and John, "Go and prepare for us the Passover lamb."
And they said, "Where do you want us to prepare it?"
He said to them, "When you enter the city, a man carrying a jar of water will meet you; follow him to the house that he enters.
And you shall say to the master of that house, 'The Teacher asks you, where is the guest room where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?'
He will show you a large upper room furnished; there make ready for us."
And they went and found it just as he had said to them, and they prepared the Passover.

sections.title: Concerning the hidden sacrifice.

verses.text: And when the hour had come, our Lord Jesus sat at the table; and the twelve disciples also sat with Him.
And He said to them, “With great desire I have desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer.
But He said to them, “I tell you, I will not eat of it until it is fulfilled in the kingdom of God.”
And He took the cup, and gave thanks; and He said, “Take this and divide it among yourselves.
For I say to you, I will not drink of the fruit of the vine until the kingdom of God comes.”
And He took bread, gave thanks, and broke it, and gave it to them, saying, “This is My body which is given for you; do this in remembrance of Me.”
Likewise, after supper, He took the cup, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in My blood, which is shed for you.”

sections.title: A sign given concerning the one who shall be afflicted.

verses.text: "But behold, a man who gives me a hand, is with me in the midst of my enemies."
"The son of man goes as it is written of him; but woe to that man by whom the son of man is betrayed."
"And the disciples began to speak among themselves, asking who it was that would do this."

sections.title: Concerning humility.

verses.text: And after this, they contended among themselves as to who should be the greatest among them.
And He said unto them, "The kings of the Gentiles exercise lordship over them; and they that exercise authority upon them are called benefactors."
But ye shall not be so; but he that is greatest among you, let him be as the younger; and he that is chief, as he that doth serve.
For whether is greater, he that sitteth at meat, or he that serveth? Is not he that sitteth at meat? But I am among you as he that serveth.
Yet ye are they which have continued with me in my temptations.
And I appoint unto you a kingdom, as my Father hath appointed unto me;
That ye may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel."

sections.title: Concerning the Strengthening of Faith

verses.text: Our Lord Jesus said, “Simon, Simon, behold, Satan has desired to sift you as wheat; but I have prayed for you, that your faith fail not; and when you are converted, strengthen your brethren.”
But I have prayed for you, that your faith may not fail; and when you have returned, strengthen your brethren.”
He said, “Lord, I am ready to go with you, both to prison and to death.”
And He said, “Peter, I tell you, the rooster shall not crow this day before you will deny three times that you know Me.”
Then He said to them, “When I sent you without money bag, knapsack, and sandals, did you lack anything?” So they said, “Nothing.”
Then He said to them, “But now, he who has a money bag, let him take it, and likewise a knapsack; and he who has no sword, let him sell his garment and buy one.”
For I say to you that this which is written must still be accomplished in Me: ‘And He was numbered with the transgressors.’ For the things concerning Me have an end.”
So they said, “Lord, look, here are two swords.” And He said to them, “It is enough.”

sections.title: Concerning the prayer of the mountain of olive.

verses.text: And he went forth to pray as he was accustomed, and he went to the Mount of Olives; and his disciples followed him.
And he said to them, “Pray that you enter not into temptation.”
And he withdrew from them about a stone's throw, and kneeling down, he prayed.
And he said, “Father, if thou be willing, remove this cup from me; nevertheless, not my will, but thine, be done.”
And there appeared an angel unto him from heaven, strengthening him.
And being in an agony, he prayed more earnestly; and his sweat was as it were great drops of blood falling down to the ground.
And when he rose up from prayer, and was come to his disciples, he found them sleeping for sorrow.
And he said unto them, “Why sleep ye? Rise and pray, lest ye enter into temptation.”

sections.title: Concerning his entrance into the hands of the Jews.

verses.text: And while he spoke these things, the people arrived; and of the twelve disciples, one was Judas, who led them; and they came to our Lord Jesus, and drew near, and the sign that was given to them was this: "Whomever I shall kiss, he is the one; take hold of him."
Our Lord Jesus said to Judas, "Will you betray the Son of Man with a kiss?"
And when they saw that they were together, they said to our Lord Jesus, "Master, will you permit us to strike them with the sword?"
And one of them struck the servant of the high priest and cut off his right ear.
But our Lord Jesus answered and said, "Put away your sword," and he touched the ear and healed him.
Our Lord Jesus said to the chief priests and the captains of the temple and the elders who had come against him, "Have you come out as against a robber, with swords and clubs?"
But I was with you daily in the temple, teaching, and you did not seize me; but this is your hour, and the power of darkness is this."

sections.title: Concerning the denial of Peter.

verses.text: And they took him to the house of the high priest; and Peter followed from afar off.
And they kindled a fire in the midst of the hall, and sat down together; and Peter sat down among them.
And as he sat by the fire and looked upon it, a certain maid beheld him; and she said, “This man was also with him.”
But he denied, saying, “Woman! I know him not.”
And after a little while another saw him and said, “Thou art also one of them.” But Peter said, “Man! I am not.”
And about the space of one hour after another confidently affirmed, saying, “Of a truth this fellow also was with him; for he is a Galilean.”
And Peter said, “Man! I know not what thou sayest.” And immediately, while he yet spake, the cock crew.
And the Lord turned and looked upon Peter; and Peter remembered the word of the Lord, how he had said unto him, “Before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice.”
And Peter went out and wept bitterly.

sections.title: The Jews, concerning their persecution against our Lord Jesus.

verses.text: Those who were with our Lord Jesus would mock Him and deride Him.
They would cover their faces and strike Him, saying, "Who is it that struck you? Tell us," as they questioned Him.
Moreover, they were speaking many other things against Him.

sections.title: Concerning the place of standing.

verses.text: And at evening, the chief priests, the scribes, and the elders of the people gathered together and took counsel against Him.
They said, “You are the Christ; tell us plainly.” And He answered them, “If I tell you, you will not believe.”
And if I ask you, you will not answer me, nor let me go.
But from now on the Son of Man shall be seated at the right hand of the power of God.”
Then all said, “Are you then the Son of God?” So He said to them, “You rightly say that I am the Son of God.”
They said, “What further testimony do we need? For we have heard it ourselves from His own mouth.”

sections.title: Our Lord stood before Pilate.

verses.text: And all rose up and went unto Pilate.
And they began to accuse Him, saying, "This man perverts the nation, and forbids to give tribute to Caesar, saying that He Himself is Christ a King."
And Pilate asked Him, "Art thou the King of the Jews?" And our Lord Jesus answered him, "Thou sayest it."
And Pilate said to the chief priests and to the people, "I find no fault in this man."
And the people cried out, saying, "He stirreth up the people, teaching throughout all Jewry, beginning from Galilee to this place."

sections.title: Our Lord before Herod, concerning His standing.

verses.text: And Pilate, hearing the word "Galilee," inquired whether the man was a Galilean.
And when he understood that He was under the jurisdiction of Herod, he sent Him to Herod; for Herod was in Jerusalem during those days.
And Herod, when he saw our Lord Jesus, was exceedingly glad; for he had desired to see Him for a long time, because he had heard many things about Him, and hoped to see some miracle done by Him.
And he questioned Him in many words; but He answered him nothing.
And the chief priests and scribes stood and vehemently accused Him.
And Herod, with his soldiers, treated Him with contempt; and mocked Him, arraying Him in a gorgeous robe, and sent Him back to Pilate.
And on that day, Herod and Pilate became friends; for before they were at enmity with each other.
And Pilate called together the chief priests and the rulers and the people.

And he said to them, "You brought this man to me as one who misleads the people; and indeed, having examined Him in your presence, I have found no fault in this man concerning those things of which you accuse Him;
nor did Herod, for I sent you back to him; and indeed, nothing deserving of death has been done by Him."
Behold, I too shall thus be cast away," he said.

sections.title: Concerning their slaying and concerning the Lord's deliverance.

verses.text: It was customary that one of the prisoners be released at every feast.
And they all cried out, saying, "Away with this man! Release unto us Barabbas!"
For Barabbas had been thrown into prison for a certain insurrection made in the city, and for murder.
Pilate, therefore, wishing to release Jesus, spoke again to them, saying, "Whom do you want me to release to you? Jesus, who is called Christ?"
But they cried out, saying, "Crucify Him! Crucify Him!"
Then Pilate said to them the third time, "Why, what evil has He done? I have found no reason for death in Him. Therefore I will chastise Him and let Him go."
But they insisted, lifting up their voices, and their voices and the voices of the chief priests prevailed.
Pilate then decided that their demand should be granted.
And he released to them the one who had been imprisoned for insurrection and murder, whom they had asked for; but he delivered Jesus to their will.

sections.title: And unto the journey of the cross.

verses.text: በወሰዱትም ጊዜ የቀሬና ሰው ስምዖንን ከዱር ሲመለስ ያዙት፤ ከጌታችን ከኢየሱስም በስተኋላ መስቀሉን አሸከሙት።
ብዙ ሰዎችም ተከተሉት፤ ሴቶችም “ዋይ ዋይ” እያሉ ያዝኑለትና ያለቅሱለት ነበሩ።
ጌታችን ኢየሱስም መለስ ብሎ እንዲህ አላቸው፥ “እናንተ የኢየሩሳሌም ልጆች ሆይ፥ ለራሳችሁና ለልጆቻችሁ አልቅሱ እንጂ ለእኔስ አታልቅሱልኝ።
መካኖች፥ ያልወለዱ ማኅፀኖችና ያላጠቡ ጡቶችም የተመሰገኑ ናቸው የሚሉበት ወራት ይመጣልና።
ያንጊዜም ተራሮችን ‘በላያችን ውደቁ፤ ኮረብቶችንም ሰውሩን’ ይሉአቸዋል።
በዚህ ርጥብ ዕንጨት እንዲህ ያደረጉ በደረቁማ እንዴት ይሆን?”

sections.title: Concerning the crucifixion with the sinners.

verses.text: And they brought two others to be crucified with Him.
And when they came to the place called Calvary, there they crucified Him; and the two others, one on the right and the other on the left, they crucified.
Our Lord Jesus said, “Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do,” and they parted His garments and cast lots.
The people stood by watching; and the rulers also mocked Him, saying, “He saved others; let Him save Himself, if He is the Christ, the chosen of God.”
And the soldiers also mocked Him, coming and offering Him sour wine.
Thus they said, “If you are the King of the Jews, save yourself.”
And an inscription also was written over Him in letters of Greek, Latin, and Hebrew: “This is the King of the Jews.”

sections.title: Concerning the two chairs.

verses.text: And one of those who were crucified with Him reviled Him, saying, "If You are the Christ, save Yourself and us."
But the other answered, rebuking him, and said, "Do you not even fear God, seeing you are under the same condemnation?"
And we indeed justly, for we receive the due reward of our deeds; but this Man has done nothing wrong."
Then he said to Jesus, "Lord, remember me when You come into Your kingdom."
And Jesus said to him, "Assuredly, I say to you, today you will be with Me in Paradise."

sections.title: The Lord concerning His death and concerning His miracles.

verses.text: ቀትር በሆነ ጊዜም በስድስት ሰዓት ፀሐይ ጨለመ፤ እስከ ዘጠኝ ሰዓት ድረስም ዓለም ሁሉ ጨለማ ሆነ።
ፀሐዩም በጨለመ ጊዜ የቤተ መቅደሱ መጋረጃ ከላይ እስከ ታች ከመካከሉ ተቀደደ።
ያንጊዜም ጌታችን ኢየሱስ ድምፁን ከፍ አድርጎ፥ “አባት ሆይ፥ ነፍሴን በአንተ እጅ አደራ እሰጣለሁ” ብሎ ጮኸ፤ ይህንም ብሎ ነፍሱን ሰጠ።
የመቶ አለቃውም የሆነውን ነገር አይቶ፥ “ይህ ሰው በእውነት ጻድቅ ነበረ”ብሎ እግዚአብሔርን አመሰገነው።
ይህንም ለማየት ተሰብስበው የነበሩት ሕዝብ ሁሉ የሆነውን ባዩ ጊዜ፥ ደረታቸውን እየመቱ ወደ ቤታቸው ተመለሱ።
የሚያውቁት ሁሉና ከገሊላ ጀምሮ የተከተሉትም ሴቶች በሩቁ ቆመው ይህን ያዩ ነበር።

sections.title: The Lord concerning His acceptance.

verses.text: እነሆ፥ በጎና ጻድቅ ሰው፥ የሸንጎ አማካሪም የሆነ ዮሴፍ የሚባል ሰው መጣ።
እርሱም በአይሁድ በምክራቸውና በሥራቸው አልተባበረም ነበር፤ ሀገሩም የይሁዳ ዕጣ የሚሆን አርማትያስ ነበር፤ እርሱም የእግዚአብሔርን መንግሥት ተስፋ ያደርግ ነበር።
ወደ ጲላጦስም ሄዶ የጌታችን የኢየሱስን ሥጋ ለመነ።
ሥጋውንም አውርዶ በበፍታ ገነዘው፤ ማንም ባልተቀበረበት፥ ከድንጋይም በተፈለፈለ መቃብር ቀበረው፤ ታላቅ ድንጋይም አንከባልሎ መቃብሩን ገጥሞ ሄደ።
ያም ቀን የሰንበት መግቢያ ዐርብ ነበር።
ከገሊላም ከእርሱ ጋር የመጡ ሁለት ሴቶች ተከትለው፥ መቃብሩን፥ ሥጋውንም እንዴት እንዳኖሩት አዩ። ተመልሰውም ሽቱና ዘይት አዘጋጁ፤ ነገር ግን በሰንበት አልሄዱም፤ ሕጋቸው እንዲህ ነበርና።

sections.title: The Lord concerning His ascension.

verses.text: And on the first day of the week, they prepared spices and went very early to the tomb; and other women were with them.
And they found the stone rolled away from the tomb.
But when they entered, they did not find the body of our Lord Jesus.
And it came to pass, as they were perplexed about this, that behold, two men stood by them in shining garments.
And as they were afraid and bowed down their faces to the earth, they said unto them, “Why seek ye the living among the dead?
He is not here, but is risen. Remember how he spake unto you when he was yet in Galilee, saying,
The Son of man must be delivered into the hands of sinful men, and be crucified, and the third day rise again.”
And they remembered his words.
And they returned from the tomb and told all these things unto the eleven and to all the rest.
It was Mary Magdalene, and Joanna, and Mary the mother of James, and other women that were with them, which told these things unto the apostles.
And this matter was to them as a parable, and they did not believe it.
And Peter arose; and he ran to the sepulcher; and stooping down, he beheld the linen clothes laid by themselves, and departed, wondering in himself at that which was come to pass.

sections.title: Concerning the people who encountered on the road to Emmaus.

verses.text: በዚያም ቀን ከመካከላቸው ሁለት ሰዎች ከኢየሩሳሌም ስድሳ ምዕራፍ ያህል ወደምትርቀው ኤማሁስ ወደምትባለው መንደር ሄዱ።
እርስ በርሳቸውም ስለ ሆነው ነገር ሁሉ ይነጋገሩ ነበር።
እነርሱም ይህን ሲነጋገሩና ሲመራመሩ ጌታችን ኢየሱስ ወደ እነርሱ ቀረበ፤ አብሮአቸውም ሄደ።
እንዳያውቁትም ዐይናቸው ተይዞ ነበር።
ጌታችንም፥ “በትካዜ እየሄዳችሁ እርስ በርሳችሁ የምትነጋገሩት ይህ ነገር ምንድን ነው?” አላቸው።
ከእነርሱም ቀለዮጳ የሚባለው አንዱ መልሶ፥ “አንተ ብቻ ለኢየሩሳሌም እንግዳ ነህን? በእነዚህ ቀኖችስ በውስጥዋ የተደረገውን አታውቅምን?” አለው።
ጌታችን ኢየሱስም፥ “ይህ ምንድነው?” አላቸው፤ እነርሱም እንዲህ አሉት፥ “በእግዚአብሔር ፊትና በሕዝቡ ሁሉ ፊት በቃሉና በሥራው ብርቱ ነቢይና እውነተኛ ሰው ስለነበረው ስለ ናዝሬቱ ስለ ኢየሱስ፥
የካህናት አለቆችና መኳንንቶቻችን አሳልፈው እንደ ሰጡት፥ ሞትም እንደ ፈረዱበትና እንደ ሰቀሉት ነው።
እኛ ግን እስራኤልን ያድናቸው ዘንድ ያለው እርሱ እንደ ሆነ ተስፋ እናደርግ ነበር፤ ከዚህም ሁሉ ጋር ይህ ነገር ከሆነ ዛሬ ሦስተኛ ቀን ነው።
ደግሞም ሴቶች ከእኛ ዘንድ ወደ መቃብር ገስግሠው ሄደው ነበርና አስደንቀው ነገሩን።
ሥጋውንም በአላገኙ ጊዜ ተመልሰው፦ ተነሥቶአል ያሉአቸውን የመላእክትን መልክ እንደ አዩ ነገሩን።
ከእኛም ዘንድ ወደ መቃብር ሄደው እንዲሁ ሴቶች እንደ ተናገሩት ሆኖ ያገኙት አሉ፤ እርሱን ግን አላዩትም።”
ጌታችን ኢየሱስም እንዲህ አላቸው፥ “እናንተ ሰነፎች፥ ነቢያትም የተናገሩትን ነገር ሁሉ ከማመን ልባችሁ የዘገየ፥
ክርስቶስ እንዲህ ይሞት ዘንድ ወደ ክብሩም ይመለስ ዘንድ ያለው አይደለምን?”
እርሱም ከሙሴና ከነቢያት፥ ከመጻሕፍትም ሁሉ ስለ እርሱ የተነገረውን ይተረጕምላቸው ጀመር።
ሊሄዱባት ወደ ነበረችው መንደርም ተቃረቡ፤ እርሱ ግን ይርቃቸው ጀመር።
እነርሱም፥ “መሽቶአልና፥ ፀሐይም ተዘቅዝቆአልና፥ ከእኛ ጋር እደር” ብለው ግድ አሉት፤ ከእነርሱም ጋር ሊያድር ገባ።
ከዚህም በኋላ አብሮአቸው ለማዕድ ተቀምጦ ሳለ እንጀራውን አንሥቶ ባረከ፤ ቈርሶም ሰጣቸው።
ዐይናቸውም ተገለጠና ዐወቁት፤ ወዲያውኑም ከእነርሱ ተሰወረ።
እርስ በርሳቸውም እንዲህ አሉ፥ “በመንገድ ሲነግረን፥ መጻሕፍትንም ሲተረጕምልን ልባችን ይቃጠልብን አልነበረምን?”

sections.title: And concerning their return unto Jerusalem.

verses.text: በዚያችም ሰዓት ተነሥተው ወደ ኢየሩሳሌም ተመለሱ፤ ዐሥራ አንዱን ደቀ መዛሙርትና አብረዋቸው የነበሩትንም ተሰብስበው አገኙአቸው፤
እንዲህ እያሉ፥ “ጌታችን በእውነት ተነሥቶአል፤ ለስምዖንም ታይቶታል።”
እነርሱም በመንገድ የሆነውንና እንጀራውን ሲቈርስ ጌታችንን እንዴት እንዳወቁት ነገሩአቸው።

sections.title: Our Lord for the revelation to His disciples.

verses.text: And while they were speaking of these things, our Lord Jesus stood in the midst of them, and said, “Peace be unto you; be not afraid; it is I.”
But they were terrified and frightened, and supposed that they had seen a spirit.
And He said unto them, “Why are you troubled? And why do thoughts arise in your hearts?
Behold my hands and my feet, that it is I myself; handle me and see; for a spirit hath not flesh and bones, as ye see me have.”
And saying this, He showed them His hands and His feet.
And while they yet believed not for joy, and wondered, He said unto them, “Have ye here any meat?”
And they gave Him a piece of a broiled fish, and of an honeycomb.
And He took it, and did eat before them.

And He said unto them, “These are the words which I spake unto you, while I was yet with you, that all things must be fulfilled, which were written in the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the psalms, concerning me.”
Then opened He their understanding, that they might understand the scriptures.
And thus He said unto them, “Christ must die, and on the third day be raised from the dead, separated from the dead.”
And it is written that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in His name, beginning at Jerusalem, and unto all nations.
And ye are witnesses of these things.
Behold, I send the promise of my Father upon you; but tarry ye in the city of Jerusalem until ye be endued with power from on high.”

sections.title: Concerning the offering.

verses.text: And He led them out as far as Bethany; and He lifted up His hands and blessed them.
And while He blessed them, He parted from them and was carried up into heaven.
And they worshipped Him, and returned to Jerusalem with great joy.
And they were continually in the temple, praising and blessing God.
